title: Deception and Ethical Boundaries
description: Some negotiators lie about bottom lines, other offers, or priorities to gain an edge. Detecting it is hard; preventing it is smarter.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: Some negotiators lie about bottom lines, other offers, or priorities to gain an edge. Detecting it is hard; preventing it is smarter.

sections.title: How It Actually Appears
content: 'I have another offer at $95K' (may be true, may be inflated).
'This is my final offer' (then later moves).
'We have several other interested parties' (could be one, could be zero).

sections.title: Warning Signs
content: They dodge when you ask for specifics ('Can you tell me more about that other offer?').
They use vague language: 'in the ballpark,' 'somewhere around.'
Their story shifts when you circle back later.

sections.title: Protection Strategy
content: Don't try to be a human lie detector; you're probably wrong.
Instead, ask diagnostic questions: 'What would you do if you were in my position?' or 'Can you put that in writing?'
Verify through independent channels whenever possible.

sections.title: Common Mistake
sections.content: Believing 'I can tell when someone is lying.' Even trained professionals perform only slightly above chance.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: Don't bet on detecting lies. Design the negotiation so deception is hard or costly for them, not easy for you to spot.
